rv.q: But the more surreal Weather Girl gets, the less assured it actually feels.
As a character study, Weather Girl sizzles.
It’s refreshing to see a piece of theater that’s both dramatically exhilarating and civically profound without ever tipping toward sanctimony.
Watkins (Epiphany) wrote the part for her, and it fits like a glove—or, to use an analogy Stacey would appreciate, a pair of sweaty Spanx.
It’s how Julia McDermott’s performance holds all the elements together, even as everything is flying apart.
Weather Girl's plot may be spotty, but it aptly captures the frantic, tense feeling often conjured by today's unrelenting news cycle.
Weather Girl is a state-of-the-nation play that delivers 70 minutes of theatrical fireworks and a dire warning.
We could all use a deliciously messed-up Weather Girl to deliver some hard truths and perhaps the hint of a miracle.

cn.t: McDermott delivers a riveting performance as a spiraling TV meteorologist in Watkins' darkly funny climate apocalypse solo show, though some critics find it more suited to television than theater.

vr.q: I really, really enjoyed this play.
I think it's one of the smartest pieces I've seen in recent memory
